# Heterogeneity and mechanism (Phase 8, RQ4)

*Generated by `python -m src.hierarchical.report` from `data/processed/hierarchical/`. Do not edit by hand. Rules: the registered plan (`docs/analysis_plan.md` at `6e24eca`, https://osf.io/jksne/) §5, read as in DEC-135, with the gaps filled before any estimate in DEC-162 to DEC-166 (pushed in `2f80dc4` before computing). Estimates are on log concentration; negative = a fall; % = 100 × (e^β − 1).*

**Read this first.** H1 is *not identified by this design* (Phase 7): the registered pre-trend test failed. So no number in this report is an effect of NCAP. The per-unit numbers are **city-level relative changes**: how a unit's satellite PM2.5 moved after listing relative to its own synthetic comparison of non-NCAP centres. H5 is a statement about those relative changes, not about where NCAP worked.

## 1. City-level estimates (DEC-162)

One synthetic difference-in-differences per NCAP unit: the unit alone against all 923 controls, with its listing cohort, log population-weighted ACAG V5.GL.06, 2010–2024 without 2020 (the primary design otherwise). H1 is not identified by this design (Phase 7, DEC-151), so this is a city-level relative change, not an effect of NCAP.

**Standard errors.** For each cohort year, every control in turn was the single fake treated unit against the other 922: the SD of those placebo estimates is the SE of every unit in that cohort (no random draws).

| cohort | treated units | placebo fits | placebo mean (log) | placebo SD = SE (log) | ± 1.96 SE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 89 | 923 | -0.0004 | 0.0487 | ±9.5 pp |
| 2020 | 15 | 923 | -0.0004 | 0.0524 | ±10.3 pp |
| 2021 | 9 | 923 | -0.0004 | 0.0524 | ±10.3 pp |

- Mean of the 113 per-unit estimates: +0.0345 (+3.5%); median +3.4%. The Phase 7 primary SDID (one synthetic comparison per cohort) is +0.0352 (+3.6%). They differ in construction, so this is orientation, not a check.
- Per-unit estimates range from -12.3% to +16.4%; 87 of 113 are above 0.
- Pre-fit-scaled SEs (sensitivity): median 0.0763, range 0.0165 to 0.2756 (cohort placebo SEs: 0.0487 to 0.0524).
- V6.GL.03 per-unit estimates correlate with V5.GL.06's at r = 0.71 across units.
- **Unshrunk city claims under Benjamini–Hochberg 5% over the 113 units (plan §5): 0 units pass.** Unadjusted, 17 have p < 0.05; the smallest p is 0.0043, and the smallest attainable with 923 placebos is 0.0022. They are not named: city-level statements come from the shrunken estimates below, and there is no best/worst table.
- Cohorts 2020 and 2021 share one placebo distribution: with 2020 dropped, both have pre-years 2010–2019 and post-years 2021–2024, so the single-unit design is identical.
- SDID convergence warnings over all 2882 V5.GL.06 fits: 0.

## 2. The hierarchical model (DEC-163)

est_i ~ Normal(θ_i, SE_i²); θ_i = α + β′x_i + τ z_i; priors α ~ N(0, 0.1), β ~ N(0, 0.05), τ ~ HalfNormal(0.05) on the log scale; NUTS, 4 chains × 2,000 draws. Intervals are 95% equal-tailed credible intervals. θ_i is a **shrunken city-level relative change**. H1 is not identified by this design (Phase 7, DEC-151), so this is a city-level relative change, not an effect of NCAP.

**Convergence** (rule: R-hat ≤ 1.01, bulk and tail ESS ≥ 400, no divergences; no number is used from a model that fails):

| model | converged | attempt | max R-hat | min bulk ESS | min tail ESS | divergences |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary: five registered moderators, cohort placebo SE, V5.GL.06 | yes | 1 | 1.002 | 2772 | 3900 | 0 |
| IGP only (IGP minus everywhere else) | yes | 1 | 1.007 | 1455 | 1709 | 0 |
| Pre-fit-scaled SE | yes | 1 | 1.003 | 3160 | 3226 | 0 |
| Prior scales x 5 | yes | 1 | 1.002 | 2811 | 4124 | 0 |
| V6.GL.03 per-unit estimates | yes | 1 | 1.002 | 3862 | 3525 | 0 |

**Primary model** (the five registered moderators; continuous moderators standardised over the 113 units):

|---|---|---|---|---|
| intercept (reference unit) | +0.0308 | +0.0122 to +0.0494 | +3.1% (+1.2% to +5.1%) | 1.000 |
| baseline PM2.5 (per SD of 2010-2018 mean log PM2.5) | -0.0193 | -0.0330 to -0.0055 | -1.9% (-3.2% to -0.5%) | 0.004 |

- Shrunken city-level relative changes: 95% CrI entirely below 0 for **1 of 113** units, entirely above 0 for **62**, spanning 0 for 50.
- Median width of a unit's 95% rank interval: 75 places out of 113 (figure 6).
- The errors of the per-unit estimates are correlated (shared donors, shared regional shocks) but the model treats them as independent, so its intervals are probably too narrow and a regional coefficient can carry a shock common to that region.

## 3. H5 (secondary): the Indo-Gangetic Plain coefficient

> **H5** (registered): effects are smaller (less negative) in IGP cities, where regional sources dominate. Rule (plan §5, read in DEC-135/164): the IGP coefficient's 95% credible interval lies entirely above 0.
>
> **The registered rule is NOT MET:** β_IGP = -0.0034 (-0.3%), 95% CrI -0.0332 to +0.0260 (-3.3% to +2.6%).
>
> H1 is not identified by this design, so β_IGP is a difference in **city-level relative changes** between IGP units and peninsular/other + north-east units with the same other moderators. It is not a difference in NCAP effects, and it says nothing about whether NCAP worked less in the IGP.

Every model (only the primary decides; DEC-164):

| model | β_IGP (log) | 95% CrI (log) | as % (95% CrI) | P(> 0) | decides H5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary: five registered moderators, cohort placebo SE, V5.GL.06 | -0.0034 | -0.0332 to +0.0260 | -0.3% (-3.3% to +2.6%) | 0.410 | yes |
| IGP only (IGP minus everywhere else) | -0.0261 | -0.0475 to -0.0043 | -2.6% (-4.6% to -0.4%) | 0.010 | no |
| Pre-fit-scaled SE | +0.0003 | -0.0373 to +0.0377 | +0.0% (-3.7% to +3.8%) | 0.512 | no |
| Prior scales x 5 | -0.0030 | -0.0342 to +0.0276 | -0.3% (-3.4% to +2.8%) | 0.434 | no |
| V6.GL.03 per-unit estimates | -0.0000 | -0.0370 to +0.0365 | -0.0% (-3.6% to +3.7%) | 0.503 | no |

*Context (Phase 7, not part of the rule):* excluding IGP units from both groups moved the Layer A estimate from +3.6% to +1.9% (+0.7% to +3.1%). IGP membership and baseline PM2.5 correlate at r = 0.70 across the 113 units, so the primary model compares IGP and other units of similar baseline pollution, while the IGP-only model does not; and its reference group also contains the coastal units. Both differences can move the IGP coefficient; which one does is not tested here. A regional coefficient also mixes in anything that happened to the whole region after 2018 (crop-residue burning, transport, weather), which the per-unit estimates share.

## 5. H3 (secondary, mechanism): PM10 vs PM2.5 on the ground

> **H3** (registered): if dust control dominated action, PM10 fell more than PM2.5 in enrolled cities, and the PM2.5/PM10 ratio rose. Labelled 'consistent with dust control' only if (i)–(iii) all hold; otherwise 'inconclusive'; never 'confirmed'.
>
> **Verdict: inconclusive.**
>
> Condition (iii) was already known to fail before this phase's rules were written (DEC-159, DEC-165), so H3 was going to be inconclusive whatever (i) and (ii) showed. Layer B is secondary, with one pre-year, and none of these is an effect of NCAP (H1 is not identified).

| condition | met |
|---|---|
| (i) log(PM2.5/PM10) estimate > 0 with 95% CI above 0, ITS and DiD (co-located stations, deweathered) | no |
| (ii) β_PM10 < β_PM2.5 and β_PM10 < 0 in ≥ 2 of 3 specifications, for both estimators | no (ITS 2 of 3; DiD 0 of 3) |
| (iii) neither Phase 7 triangulation pair is 'conflict' (DEC-150) | no (Layer A restricted vs ground DiD (like-for-like): uninformative; Layer A restricted vs ITS: conflict) |

**(ii) on the cities that hold both pollutants** (DEC-165; raw = all stations raw, deweathered = all stations deweathered, balanced panel = the Layer B primary; ITS = after listing minus before, DiD = against control-pool cities; 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs):

| specification | estimator | PM2.5 (95% CI) | PM10 (95% CI) | PM10 fell, and more | cities (single-station) / control cities |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw | ITS | -5.4% (-11.2% to +0.9%) | -6.3% (-13.4% to +1.7%) | yes | 11 (5) / 5 |
| raw | DiD (city means) | +5.5% (-4.4% to +18.1%) | +10.3% (-0.5% to +23.2%) | no | 11 (5) / 5 |
| deweathered | ITS | -4.6% (-10.8% to +3.0%) | -4.6% (-9.8% to +1.2%) | no | 11 (5) / 5 |
| deweathered | DiD (city means) | +4.3% (-4.4% to +14.1%) | +7.6% (-1.1% to +19.1%) | no | 11 (5) / 5 |
| balanced panel | ITS | -1.2% (-7.1% to +4.5%) | -5.1% (-10.9% to +0.6%) | yes | 11 (9) / 5 |
| balanced panel | DiD (stations) | +0.7% (-6.6% to +17.8%) | +3.2% (-3.0% to +16.0%) | no | 11 (9) / 5 |

**(i) the ratio**, on stations in both strict 2018 panels:

*Scope:* the cities with both pollutants are a subset of Layer B's 18 (PM2.5) and 13 (PM10) cities, mostly single stations, against 5 control cities. The audit's missingness bias on annual means (median +0.5 to +0.7%) applies. Ground PM10 is never set against satellite PM2.5 as agreement.

## 6. Funding dose-response (EXPLORATORY; DEC-166)

*Exploratory, not a hypothesis test.* H1 is not identified by this design (Phase 7, DEC-151), so this relates city-level relative changes, not effects of NCAP, to money. Dose = XV Finance Commission air-quality **allocation** (FY2020-21 + FY2021-26) per person, not releases: XV-FC releases reward cities that improved (reverse causality). Allocations avoid that link but not every reverse-causal path.

- Units with a dose: **40** NCAP units (all their cities XV-FC, matched to an allocation row). Excluded: Badlapur, Ulhasnagar (no allocation row of its own); Delhi, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida (a member city is in the NCAP channel). NCAP-channel cities have no allocation table in the extracted documents, so they have no dose.
- Dose range: Rs 782 to Rs 3,746 per person (median Rs 1,576).
- **Per-person allocations are set largely state by state:** in the 11 states with two or more UAs, the within-state range is a median 0.7% of the state mean (maximum 1.5%), while state means run from Rs 788 to Rs 3,746. So the dose is confounded with state and region.

| model | units | per doubling of the dose (log) | as % (95% CrI) | P(> 0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| log dose | 40 | -0.0043 | -0.4% (-3.5% to +2.7%) | 0.395 |
| log dose + IGP | 40 | +0.0008 | +0.1% (-3.1% to +3.3%) | 0.521 |
| log dose, without the highest-dose unit (Patna) | 39 | +0.0061 | +0.6% (-2.7% to +4.1%) | 0.641 |
